subject: Candidate borrowed callable non-copying boundary
claim: The candidate typed verifier rejects borrowed callable copies, including nested array and Option contents, while retaining exact borrowed indirect invocation. All 217 focused groups pass on Windows; complete WVB 1.39 admission remains disabled.

source.value: Worktree based on a87c747587aad95cc8b662dcadcbb832e239ef68. Exact changed implementation and test inputs follow; unchanged dependencies and bootstrap tools belong to that commit.

runs.target: Existing 217 Foundation borrow-owner groups; callable composition groups 193, 194, and 197 now contain seven rejection probes (two corrected expectations and five added probes). Retained positive cases cover exact direct, array-element, and Option-view invocation, nominal mismatch rejection, and ordinary callable aggregate construction.

limitations: This is component verification, not source publication, candidate runtime execution, complete admission, or cross-host qualification. No runtime retention behavior is claimed.

A callable descriptor proves exact invocation identity, not Copy ownership. The candidate read-through proof conservatively rejects callable contents; this does not introduce a general affine callable implementation or alter earlier bytecode versions.
The existing grouped inventory remains 217; it is not a count of individual assertions. Existing owner, lifetime, metadata, and call checks were executed, not replaced by a new verifier.

An initial build failed in about 3.3 seconds on an extra closing parenthesis introduced by this edit. It was corrected before the reported passing construction and execution. Failed evidence is not a pass.

The proposed broad changed-file plan selected 12 native owners at 2925 expected seconds and 11700 maximum seconds. It was not run because it exceeds the ten-minute local budget. Full compiler front-door, bootstrap, complete callable execution, runtime, ABI, OS, and Linux qualification were not run.
Broader owned-payload handling, complete admission audit, runtime retention, exclusive borrowing, take, mapping, and real consumer migration remain open.
No clean-machine performance comparison or peak working-set measurement was performed. Existing bounded traversal is retained; the change adds no allocation or new traversal.
